analysis:
This PR is documentation-only. docs/developer/test.md changes the 'Last updated' stamp (line 3) and adds a paragraph at lines 837-842. The paragraph describes scripts/test-provider-release-publication.py: isolated local Git tags, multiline/CRLF/blank-line annotations, synthetic SSH/PGP signature armor, exact retained note text and digest guards, and no signing or live publication. docs/operations/provider-release.md changes the date stamp, adds a note near line 149 that release_changelog strips only Git's identified signature suffix and trims outer whitespace, and updates table row 6 (line 463) to say original tag notes without the signature suffix. No source, workflow, key-handling, attestation, WebSocket, encryption, cache, or fan-helper code changes appear in the supplied evidence.

I checked the changes against the threat model. The relevant themes are A-005/A-011 release registration and build-identity integrity, T-054 (unqualified or revoked build accepted via stale code evidence) and T-034. The docs describe release-note preservation and test hygiene: tests use local tags and synthetic armor, with no secrets or production calls. They do not weaken a documented control. The statement that digest guards remain, and that the 64 KiB registration limit still applies, is consistent with the existing text.

The actual change to scripts/provider-release-publication.py (release_changelog behavior) and the new test script are not in the supplied evidence. I therefore cannot verify that the docs match the implementation, for example that signature stripping cannot truncate legitimate note content or that registration payload digests stay bound. That is a documentation-accuracy question for whoever reviews the script change, not a finding here. I found no regression or invalidated assumption.
